newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-BRAZIL CLUB SUSPENDED, TWO BANNED FOR LIFE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BRAZIL CLUB SUSPENDED, TWO BANNED FOR LIFE.

text.p: Brazilian soccer club Atletico Paranaense have been suspended for 360 days and two men banned for life following a corruption scandal, a Brazilian Football Confederation (CBF) official said on Friday.

Mario Celso Petraglia, president of Atletico Paranaense, and Ivens Mendes, former CBF refereeing director, were banned from any soccer-related activity by a CBF tribunal, Martinho de Oliveira Filho, the tribunal's secretary, said.

The club and the two directors were found guilty of breaking various regulations which deal with using the game in their own benefit. Alberto Dualib, president of the Corinthians club, was suspended for two years for breaking the same regulations, Oliveira said.
The scandal blew up last month with allegations that Mendes had used his post to exchange favours with club directors to fuel his campaign to be elected to the Brazilian Congress.

Mendes resigned in early May amid media allegations he had offered to ask a referee to give Atletico Paranaense a helping hand in a Copa Brasil match they were to play in exchange for 25,000 Real ($23,600).

The allegations were based on recordings played by the Globo television station. Globo said the recordings, which it was sent anonymously, were of phone conversations involving Mendes and Petraglia and Mendes and Dualib.
Thursday's judgment was held following a two-week inquiry by the CBF into the affair.
Dozens of Atleico Paranaense fans gathered outside the CBF's headquarters to await the verdict, having undegone a 16-hour bus journey from the southern city of Curitiba where the club is based.
The ban was celebrated by fans of Fluminense, relegated in the Brazilian championship last year. They are hoping their team will be able to fill a possible gap led by Atletico's ban.
Fluminense fans also gathered in front of the building and police at one stage had to separate the two sides.
